newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FIXED BOND YIELD SEEN RISING AT TENDER.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FIXED BOND YIELD SEEN RISING AT TENDER.

text.p: Poland's 200 million zloty 12-percent five-year bond auction on Thursday is likely to be heavily oversubscribed with large foreign investor demand amid expectations of higher yields, analysts said on Wednesday.

Analysts said the maximum yield of the bonds, which come from a previous treasury offer and mature in just over four years, could rise as high as 19.5 percent on Thursday from 18.5 percent at the last five-year bond auction on February 5.
They said foreign interest would be boosted by the zloty's half percentage point plunge on Wednesday caused by several waves of central bank currency-buying interventions.

"Bids from foreign investors with longer investment horizons should cover most of the treasury's offer on Thursday, as the central bank's interventions made potential investment in Polish paper cheaper," said a dealer at a London bank.
At the last fixed bond auction foreigners bought some 60 percent of the 552 million zlotys of five-year bonds sold.
Analysts said the treasury may cut minimum prices of its bonds after trimming the minimum price of its benchmark 52-week T-bill by 0.26 to 82.90 at last Monday's tender.
They expected total demand to reach 400 million zlotys at Thursday's 200 million zloty tender.

The bonds on auction tomorrow mature on June 12, 2001 and come from an earlier three billion zloty issue of 12-percent five-year bonds, from which 1.736 billion was sold at four consecutive tenders from February to May of last year.
The value date for this tender will be March 5, 1997. The deadline for the auction is 1200 local time (1100 GMT). The next auction of the paper is scheduled for March 20, 1997.
